description: Makassarpleinbuurt 1925-26 perimeter blocks (Molukkenstraat 7-29, Boetonstraat 6-20, Niasstraat 3-13 and 17-27): a flat-roofed 6.0-6.5 m brick front, three white-framed windows with a gridded toplight on each of three equal storeys, a closing top storey of three small square attic lights high under the roof, a darker ground storey with paired house doors at the party walls; a plain parapet with a thin light coping, or (Niasstraat) a deep flat eaves overhang with a white fascia

match.note: flat roof at 14.4-14.9 m, BAG 1925-26, three axes on ~6.2 m; the row of square attic lights 1.5-2 m under the roof line is what tells it from the white-attic type (Gorontalostraat 25-45, eaves 12.7 m)

parapet.note: Molukkenstraat 7-29, Boetonstraat 6-20: plain brick parapet over the attic lights, a thin light coping at 14.8-15.2 m

overhang.note: Niasstraat 3-13 (and 17-27): a deep flat eaves overhang with a white fascia over the attic lights; its soffit reads brown in the shade

door-left.note: house doors at the left party wall (paired with the neighbour's), two windows beside them

door-right.note: house doors at the right party wall

rhythm.bays: 3 equal axes; the attic storey's three small lights on the same axes
rhythm.symmetry: symmetric above the ground; doors pair across party walls
rhythm.groundFloor: paired house doors at a party wall, or a shop (Molukkenstraat)
rhythm.roofline: flat: plain parapet with a light coping, or a deep eaves overhang (Niasstraat)

schemaLimits: the darker ground-storey brick and the soldier-course ledge over it
the doors stand on the first/last axis, not against the party wall, and a pair is drawn as one door
the small brick header accents at the storey lines (Boetonstraat)
